rows.question: i have [[Hardened Scales]] and [[Doubling Season]] and cast ballista for X=2. how many counters does it come in with? do i get to pick the order or is it timestamps
rows.expected_answer: You choose the order and the best answer is 6. Walking Ballista's 'enters with X +1/+1 counters' is a replacement effect (614.1c, 614.12), and Hardened Scales and Doubling Season are further replacement effects modifying the same event. When multiple replacement effects apply to the same event, the affected permanent's controller picks which applies first (616.1), and since none of the special priorities in 616.1a-d apply, any may be chosen (616.1e). Each effect applies only once to the event (614.5). Apply Scales first (2 -> 3), then Season doubles (3 -> 6). Timestamps are irrelevant for replacement effects; that is the layer system for continuous effects.

outcome.answer: You choose the order, and it is not by timestamp. Ordering Hardened Scales first gives **Walking Ballista** 6 counters, while Doubling Season first gives 5. Both replacement effects modify the counters the Ballista enters with. The affected object's controller picks which applicable effect applies next (616.1), and any applicable one may be chosen (616.1e). Starting from the 2 counters printed by X=2: Hardened Scales first gives 2+1=3, then Doubling Season doubles that to 6. Doubling Season first gives 2×2=4, then Hardened Scales adds one for 5. Choose Hardened Scales first for 6. The ruling on two counter effects on one creature you control confirms you pick the order.

rows.question: opp cast [[Blood Moon]] while i have all three tron lands out. do i still get my 7 mana from urza's? can i tap tower for 3 colorless or is it just a Mountain now
rows.expected_answer: Tron is off. Blood Moon is a type-changing effect (layer 4, 613.1d) that sets each nonbasic land's subtype to Mountain. Per 305.7, a land whose subtype is set to a basic land type loses its old land types (so it is no longer an Urza's land), loses all abilities from its rules text (the colorless mana ability), and gains only '{T}: Add {R}'. Each Urza's land is a plain Mountain that taps for one red mana; Tower does not produce three because it no longer has that ability and the others no longer have the Urza's subtype. They are still nonbasic (305.8), so Blood Moon keeps affecting them.

outcome.answer: No, you don't get 7 mana, and Urza's Tower can't tap for {C}{C}{C}. **Blood Moon** is a layer 4 type-changing effect (613.1d) that makes each nonbasic land a Mountain. Each Tron land loses its other land types and its printed abilities, so **Urza's Tower**, **Urza's Mine** and **Urza's Power Plant** each become a Mountain with only "{T}: Add {R}". Each one taps for a single {R}. The Urza's ability checks land types, not names, and the lands are no longer Urza's Mine, Urza's Power-Plant or Urza's Tower, so the 3-mana and 2-mana conditions can never be met. The lands keep their names and stay nonbasic, but that doesn't matter for mana production.

rows.question: follow up: what if I play [[Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth]] AFTER the moon is already down? urborg has the later timestamp so shouldn't it make everything a Swamp too? my friend says no
rows.expected_answer: Your friend is right. Both effects are layer 4 type-changing effects (613.1d). Urborg's effect depends on Blood Moon's (613.8a): applying Blood Moon makes Urborg a Mountain and strips its rules-text ability (305.7), which removes the existence of Urborg's effect. When a dependency exists it overrides timestamps (613.8), so Blood Moon applies first no matter which entered later (613.8b). Urborg is just a Mountain with '{T}: Add {R}' and nothing becomes a Swamp. (Any actual basic Swamps you control are still Swamps because Blood Moon only affects nonbasic lands.)

outcome.answer: Your friend is right: Urborg's later timestamp doesn't help. Blood Moon makes Urborg a nonbasic Mountain, and a land that gets a new land type this way loses the abilities from its rules text, so Urborg's ability (which grants Swamp to each land) no longer exists. Blood Moon's effect changes whether Urborg's effect exists, so Urborg's effect depends on Blood Moon's. Per 613.8b, a dependent effect waits until the effects it depends on have applied, so timestamp order never comes into play. Result: Urborg is just a Mountain with '{T}: Add {R}', and the other lands are not Swamps. Both effects are in layer 4 (613.1d), but the dependency rule overrides the timestamp.

rows.question: my goyf has two +1/+1 counters on it and I just giant growthed it. opponent [[Clone]]s it. is their clone a huge goyf too or just a regular one? and does the clone even know how big a goyf should be since the p/t is */*+1
rows.expected_answer: Just a regular Tarmogoyf. A copy acquires only the copiable values of the original (707.2): name, mana cost, types, rules text, printed P/T, etc. Counters, Giant Growth's +3/+3, and other non-copy effects are not copiable values, so the Clone gets none of them. The Clone does copy Tarmogoyf's rules text, and therefore its characteristic-defining ability (707.2a), so the Clone's own P/T is */*+1 computed from card types in graveyards (applied in layer 7a, 613.4a). The copy effect itself is applied in layer 1a (613.2a); your goyf's counters and pump are layer 7c (613.4c) and stay on your goyf only.

outcome.answer: Their Clone is a regular Tarmogoyf, not a huge one. Copy effects copy only copiable values, and per 707.2 counters and other effects are not copied: "Other effects (including type-changing and text-changing effects), status, counters, and stickers are not copied." Your two +1/+1 counters and the +3/+3 from Giant Growth stay with your Goyf. The Clone does know how to size itself because its copied rules text includes the characteristic-defining ability. Per 707.2a, "those values are derived from its rules text," so the Clone's power is the number of card types among cards in all graveyards and its toughness is that number plus 1, counted as of now. It is a Tarmogoyf with no counters, so its stats are just the graveyard count.

rows.question: ok classic one. I have [[Humility]] out and my opponent drops [[Opalescence]]. what are Humility and Opalescence now?? are all my creatures still 1/1? does the answer change if Opalescence was out first?
rows.expected_answer: Walk the layers. Opalescence reads 'each OTHER non-Aura enchantment', so it never affects itself: Opalescence stays a noncreature enchantment and keeps its ability in every scenario. Layer 4 (613.1d): Opalescence makes Humility a 'creature' enchantment. Layer 6 (613.1f): Humility removes all abilities from every creature, including itself; per 613.6 an effect that has started applying keeps applying in later layers even though its source ability is gone. Layer 7b (613.4b): Humility's 'base P/T 1/1' and Opalescence's 'base P/T equal to mana value' both set Humility's P/T. Neither depends on the other under 613.8a (applying one doesn't change the text, existence, or targets of the other), so timestamp order decides (613.7). If Opalescence has the later timestamp: Humility is a 4/4 creature with no abilities. If Humility has the later timestamp: Humility is a 1/1 creature with no abilities. Either way every ordinary creature is a 1/1 with no abilities, and Opalescence is an unaffected noncreature enchantment. Any other non-Aura enchantment Opalescence animates follows Humility itself: its base power and toughness are its mana value when Opalescence is later, and 1/1 when Humility is.

outcome.answer: Humility's controller's non-enchantment creatures are always 1/1 with no abilities. Opalescence only changes enchantments, so it does not touch them. Opalescence itself stays an enchantment with its ability, because it does not affect itself ("other"). **Humility** is the one that gets tangled up: Opalescence makes it a creature with base P/T equal to its mana value, and Humility then loses all its abilities in layer 6. The two competing base P/T settings in layer 7b are applied in timestamp order, so the later one wins (613.4b, 613.7). With Humility out first and Opalescence entering later, Humility is 4/4 with no abilities, and any other enchantment Opalescence animates is at its mana value. If Opalescence was out first, Humility's later timestamp makes it 1/1 with no abilities, so yes, the answer changes for Humility itself. Humility losing its abilities does not stop Opalescence's effect, because that effect started applying in layer 4 and continues in later layers (613.6).

rows.question: quick one: if I have [[Valki, God of Lies]] in hand can I just cast the Tibalt side for 7? and while it's in my library/graveyard does it count as a planeswalker card for stuff like Vraska's Contempt / Kaya's Ghostform?
rows.expected_answer: Yes. Valki // Tibalt is a modal double-faced card: when you cast it you choose which face you're casting before it goes on the stack, and only that face is evaluated (712.11b, 712.11c), so you can cast Tibalt, Cosmic Impostor for {5}{B}{R} straight from your hand. Once chosen, the spell/permanent has only that face's characteristics (712.8f). But anywhere other than the stack or battlefield (hand, library, graveyard, exile) an MDFC has only its front face's characteristics (712.8a), so it is a legendary creature card named Valki, God of Lies there — never a planeswalker card.

outcome.answer: Yes. **Valki, God of Lies** is a modal double-faced card, so when you cast it from hand you choose which face to cast, and you pay that face's cost: {5}{B}{R}, which is 7 mana (712.11b). No, it doesn't count as a planeswalker card in your library or graveyard. A double-faced card in those zones has only the characteristics of its front face (712.8a), so it's Valki, a creature card. Vraska's Contempt and Kaya's Ghostform only matter on the battlefield. There, once Tibalt resolves it is a planeswalker, Vraska's Contempt can exile it, and Kaya's Ghostform can enchant it if you control it.

rows.question: cast Stomp off my bonecrusher giant, it resolved and went to exile. my opp says I can only cast the creature half from exile now, not Stomp again, is that right? also can they counter Stomp with a 'counter target creature spell' effect since the card is a creature?
rows.expected_answer: Your opponent is right. When an Adventure spell resolves it is exiled instead of going to the graveyard, and you may cast the card from exile — but only as the creature (Bonecrusher Giant), not as Stomp again (715.3d). And no, Stomp can't be hit by 'counter target creature spell': while on the stack as an Adventure the spell has only its alternative characteristics (715.3a, 715.3b), so it is a red instant, not a creature spell. Everywhere else, including exile, the card is just the creature card Bonecrusher Giant (715.4).

outcome.answer: Your opponent is right about exile, but you can still cast the creature. Per 715.3d, Stomp can't be cast again from exile as an Adventure. You may play Bonecrusher Giant from exile as a permanent spell, subject to its normal timing. They can't counter Stomp with a 'counter target creature spell' effect. While Stomp is on the stack it has only its Adventure characteristics (715.3b), so it's an instant spell, not a creature spell, and that effect can't target it. A 'counter target spell' effect could still counter it.
citations: rule 715.3d: "It can’t be cast as an Adventure this way, although other effects that allow a player to cast it may allow a player to cast it as an Adventure."
ruling d6d72f5f-8f5d-4180-b514-f22ff5482902/9f9546560bbab6ce: "For as long as it remains exiled, that player may cast it as a permanent spell."

rows.question: melded my Bruna and Gisela into Brisela and then it got Path to Exiled. does that count as one creature leaving or two for my [[Blood Artist]] type triggers, and do I get one Plains or two off Path?
rows.expected_answer:
Blood Artist does not trigger at all here: Path to Exile exiles Brisela, and Blood Artist
triggers on a creature dying, which means being put into a graveyard from the battlefield
(700.4). Exile is not dying. If Brisela instead died (say, to a Wrath of God), Blood Artist
would trigger exactly once: one permanent left the battlefield, even though the melded

rows.expected_answer: Your buddy is half right. After you cast a spell you receive priority again (117.3c), so you may cast the second Bolt immediately, before he can respond to the first. Nothing resolves until all players pass in succession with the stack non-empty (117.4); then only the top object resolves, and the active player gets priority again after it resolves (117.3b). outcome.answer: Yes. You keep priority after casting, so you can cast a second Bolt before he gets a chance to respond to the first. Your buddy is right that he can't respond until you pass, but you don't have to pass after the first Bolt. Casting a spell gives you priority afterward (117.3c), and he only gets priority once you pass (117.3d). The second Bolt, cast while the first is on the stack, resolves first (117.7). Both Bolts are instants, so you can cast them whenever you have priority (117.1a). Note that Lightning Bolt doesn't counter anything; it deals 3 damage to any target, so he would need his own instant-speed response to interact with either spell.

rows.question: I control a 2/2 with a Giant Growth resolving on it, and mid-resolution of a different spell it's technically at 0 toughness for a second (Maro-style hand-size thing). Does it die? And separately, if I have two Ragavan on the battlefield somehow, when exactly does the legend rule kick in - can I respond in between?
rows.expected_answer: 1) It doesn't die. State-based actions are only checked when a player would receive priority, not in the middle of a spell resolving (704.3, 704.4 - the CR's own Maro example). The creature only dies if it still has toughness 0 or less when SBAs are next checked (704.5f). 2) The legend rule (704.5j) is also a state-based action: the moment a player would get priority with two Ragavans you control, you choose one and the other goes to the graveyard. It doesn't use the stack and there is no window to respond between the second Ragavan entering and the legend rule applying; you can only respond before the second one enters/resolves.

outcome.answer: No, it doesn't die. State-based actions are not checked during resolution, so a creature that is at 0 toughness mid-resolution is put into the graveyard only if it still has 0 toughness when they are next checked, which is when a player would next get priority (per 704.4 and 704.3). A plain 2/2 only reaches 0 toughness through a toughness-reducing effect, and Giant Growth's +3/+3 would make it 5/5 on resolution anyway. Scryfall's Maro ruling confirms the timing. On the legend rule, it is a state-based action (704.5j). State-based actions are performed as a single event before any player gets priority, so with two **Ragavan** on the battlefield the legend rule applies as soon as the condition exists. The controller chooses one and the other goes to the graveyard. You cannot respond between the condition arising and the legend rule being applied. Only after it is applied do waiting triggers go on the stack and priority is given out.

rows.question: commander q: my commander is [[Kenrith, the Returned King]]. two things: 1) can I run Nicol Bolas, the Ravager since Kenrith's text mentions all 5 colors? and 2) someone bounced Kenrith to my hand with Unsummon - does he go to the command zone or is that only for graveyard/exile?

rows.question: two quick ones. 1) if I tap all my lands during my upkeep does that mana stick around so I can cast the mind sculptor in my main phase? 2) when I'm casting snappy can I tap lands in the middle of casting it or do I have to float the mana first?
rows.expected_answer: 1) No. Each player's mana pool empties at the end of each step and phase, so mana added during your upkeep is lost before your main phase (106.4). Tap the lands in your main phase instead. 2) Yes. Casting a spell includes a step where, if the total cost includes mana, you get a chance to activate mana abilities such as tapping lands (601.2g), and only then do you pay the total cost (601.2h). You do not need to float mana before announcing the spell.

outcome.answer: 1) No. Each player's mana pool empties at the end of each step and phase, so mana you tap for in your upkeep is lost before your main phase (per 106.4). While casting **Snapcaster Mage**, after targets are chosen and the total cost is determined, you get a chance to activate mana abilities (per 601.2g), so you can tap lands during casting. Mana abilities must be activated before costs are paid, and you may activate them whenever you are casting a spell that requires a mana payment (per 605.3a).

rows.question: i have [[Academy Manufactor]] and [[Shelob, Child of Ungoliant]] out. a creature my spider hit dies and shelob makes a token copy of it that's a food. with manufactor out do i get the food copy plus a clue and a treasure, or what happens?
rows.expected_answer: No copy. Academy Manufactor's "instead" makes it a replacement effect (614.1a), and Shelob's trigger would create a Food token, so Manufactor applies. The replaced event never happens (614.6): instead of the Food that would be a copy of the creature, you create one Clue, one Food and one Treasure token. Those are predefined tokens with only their standard characteristics (111.10a, 111.10b, 111.10f). 111.10 lets the effect that creates a predefined token modify it, but Shelob's modifications belonged to the replaced event, and Manufactor's own effect modifies nothing. You end up with a plain Food, a plain Clue and a plain Treasure, and the creature is not copied.

outcome.answer: You get a Clue, a Food and a Treasure, but not a copy of the creature. Shelob's trigger would create a Food token, and **Academy Manufactor** replaces that creation: per 614.1a the word "instead" makes it a replacement effect, and per 614.6 the original token creation never happens. Instead you create one Clue, one Food and one Treasure. The copy's characteristics belonged to the replaced event, so the Food you get is an ordinary Food with no copied creature and no copied abilities. Because the replaced event never happens, the creature's enters-the-battlefield abilities don't trigger from it. The Food's sacrifice-for-life ability from Shelob's text is also not given to it. Per the Scryfall rulings, the Clue created this way is not investigating, so investigate triggers won't fire.

rule 614.6: "If an event is replaced, it never happens. A modified event occurs instead, which may in turn trigger abilities."
